title.narrative: Promotion of a green and circular economy through civil society engagement and good governance in highly urbanized coastal cities in the Philippines

description.narrative:
The project is designed with the purpose of improving and strengthening the capacities of civil society, communities, local authorities, and vulnerable informal sectors workers, in order to foster an enabling environment that is conducive to the meaningful participation and positive progress towards the National Action Plan on Marine Litter and linked legislation in the Philippines, the ASEAN Regional Action Plan for Combating Marine Debris, and in line with Part XII of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)

The project will support efforts to promote a conducive setting for meaningful and structured participation of CSOs in the improvement of Circular Economy in the Philippines, and specifically the ban on single-use plastic and the integration of Informal Waste workers legislations, policies and institutional frameworks, by increasing the CSOs capacity to perform their roles as independent development actors more effectively in increasing the awareness on Circular Economy and the risk of single-use plastic, as well as establish coordinated mechanisms to integrate Informal Waste Collectors and promote their work as actors of change as well as to enhance the efficiency of the local government units (LGU) solid waste management sector.

The project will work towards improving and promote Circular Economy at community level, in particular the mitigation of plastic waste contamination in marine environments, through the transition from single-use plastic items to highly reusable, retrievable, recyclable, or compostable alternatives and plastic-reduction schemes and support the planning efforts of local actors of governance, organized and fully integrated through this Action, targeting in particular the informal sector and local communities most exposed to plastic contamination and its effects.
